subject: Clarify: training assurances and data disposal playbook
messages:
From: Tim Bennett <tim.bennett@olivehealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions: training assurances + deletion timeline

Hi Nikhil,

Quick follow up from the security review: our legal team needs explicit answers to two items for the contract and the data map before we can proceed. Can you confirm the following for Redwood-hosted inference used by OliveHealth?

1) "Training usage" assurance: Do you train models on customer request payloads, embeddings, or logs? If not, please state precisely which data classes are excluded from any training/weight-update processes and which (if any) telemetry might be used for aggregate model improvements.

2) Deletion & retention nuances: We need a short playbook describing how data is deleted on request (including backups, object storage, KV caches, prefix/KV cache used by the runtime, embeddings store, audit logs, and offline backups). Please include the expected timeline for each data class and how you provide proof of deletion.

We appreciate a concise response we can attach as an exhibit for procurement. If you have a short playbook PDF or a reference link, please include.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Bennett
Senior Counsel, OliveHealth

Subject: Re: Questions: training assurances + deletion timeline

Tim — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise, contract-ready summary plus an immediate next step (we attached a short playbook PDF). I kept the language precise so legal can paste into the exhibit.

1) Training on customer data
- Short answer: Redwood does not use customer prompt/response payloads, customer-provided embeddings, or customer metadata to train or update model weights for our public or internal models.
- Scope & specifics: This exclusion applies to: request/response text, embeddings generated for or uploaded by the customer, customer-provided model artifacts, and metadata (customer IDs, request IDs) tied to those payloads.
- Telemetry & aggregated signals: Redwood collects operational telemetry (e.g., request latencies, error rates, token-level counts) and aggregated usage statistics to improve system reliability and capacity planning. Such telemetry is aggregated and de-identified; it is not linked to customer identifiers and is not used to train model weights. Any research experiments that use anonymized logs require explicit opt-in and are governed by a separate data use agreement.

2) Deletion & retention playbook (high level) — attached PDF contains the full steps. Highlights:
- Active data (live request/response payloads): purged on customer request within 24–72 hours from hosted subsystems, depending on the pipeline in flight.
- KV/prefix/cache (runtime caches, KV cache for autoregressive decoding): caches are in-memory or ephemerally persisted to local instance storage. On deletion request we trigger an immediate eviction and rotation of instance storage; expected window: within 24 hours.
- Embeddings index/store: embeddings created by the customer are stored in a dedicated object store/index that supports per-customer segmentation. Deletion action removes the index entries and connected vector shards; expected window: 3–14 days depending on shard compaction schedules.
- Backups & snapshots (object storage & DB backups): retention windows vary by plan. For hosted customers, backups are scheduled and are eligible for deletion on request; the playbook specifies targeted snapshot invalidation and zeroing procedures — expected window: up to 30 days to guarantee removal from all cold storage copies.
- Audit logs & security logs: retained per our SOC2 retention schedule (default 90 days). We can negotiate shorter retention for enterprise plans with a contract amendment.
- Model cache / compiled kernels / ephemeral artifacts: these do not contain customer data beyond empty runtime traces and are rotated on version changes; no long-term storage of payloads.

Proof-of-deletion and verification:
- We provide a deletion certificate with: (a) time-stamped action record, (b) list of object keys/IDs removed, (c) hash references where applicable, and (d) an internal audit ticket ID. For backup/snapshot deletion that requires a longer window, the certificate indicates the completion time and the storage regions affected.

Contract language we suggest (single sentence):
"Redwood will not use Customer Data (including request/response payloads and Customer-generated embeddings) to train, fine-tune, or benchmark models without the Customer's explicit, written opt-in. Redwood will, upon Customer request, delete Customer Data as described in the attached Data Deletion Playbook and provide a signed Deletion Certificate."

Next steps: attached is our Data Deletion Playbook v1 (short). Laura — can you review the contract sentence and confirm whether we should extend shorter audit-log retention for OliveHealth?

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: training assurances + deletion timeline

Tim — adding two small edits we typically include in an exhibit and flagging negotiation levers.

Edited contract sentence (recommended for legal):
"Redwood will not use Customer Data (including request/response payloads, customer-provided embeddings, and associated metadata) to train, fine-tune, or benchmark models without the Customer's explicit, written opt-in. Redwood may collect aggregated, de-identified operational telemetry for system reliability and capacity planning; such telemetry will not be used to update model weights. Upon Customer request, Redwood will execute deletion actions per the Data Deletion Playbook and provide a signed Deletion Certificate specifying affected artifacts and completion timestamps."

Negotiation points you may see:
- Audit log retention: default 90 days; we can offer 30 days with an enterprise addendum.
- Backup deletion window: we guarantee initiation of removal within 30 days; some cold backups may require additional verification steps.
- Proof-of-deletion format: we can provide signed certificates plus an optional third-party attestation for an SOW fee.

If that language looks good, we can attach the playbook and the SOC2 excerpt as exhibits. Marissa — can you prepare the exhibit bundle and the short summary for procurement?

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
